clue.text: Where soldiers save joints of meat?

parts.note: save in its old sense of except or but, as in 'all save one', which is also bar
a rack is a joint of lamb or pork cut from the ribs, so racks are joints of meat

explanation.surface: A question about troops putting aside cuts of meat for later.
explanation.walkthrough: 'save' looks like a verb about hoarding, but it is the preposition meaning except.
explanation.definitionFit: Barracks are the buildings in which soldiers are housed, so they are where soldiers live.

clue.text: Really go all out to write a narrative

indicators.note: all out suggests the letters of Really go are completely disordered

explanation.surface: An instruction to make a real effort writing a story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'all out' looks like full effort, but it signals rearranging REALLY GO.
explanation.definitionFit: An allegory is a story with a hidden moral or political meaning.

clue.text: Recovery expected in about thirty years

parts.note: re means about or concerning, as in business letters
a generation is reckoned at roughly thirty years

explanation.surface: A forecast that a slump will take three decades to turn around.
explanation.definitionFit: Regeneration is renewal or revival after decline, as in urban regeneration.

parts.note: the food is something you eat, and the same word is what a photographer tells you to say so that you smile

explanation.surface: An order to eat up and smile about it.
explanation.walkthrough: Photographers ask people to say this word because it shapes the mouth into a grin.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a dairy food made from milk curds, and saying it for a camera makes you smile.

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: Ras is the title of an Ethiopian prince or chief, as in Ras Tafari
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: An instruction to dress up an Ethiopian prince.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dress up' looks like one phrase, but 'Dress' is the definition and 'up' reverses RAS to SAR.
explanation.definitionFit: A sari is a long draped garment worn by women in South Asia.

indicators.note: in, with surroundings, says the royal letter sits within the other word
surroundings says the word for beastly goes round the royal letter

parts.note: piggish means behaving like a pig, beastly and greedy
R stands for rex or regina, the king or queen

explanation.surface: A devout king living among brutish people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in ... surroundings' puts R inside PIGGISH, giving P-R-IGGISH.
explanation.definitionFit: Priggish means smugly self-righteous, the sanctimonious sense of pious.

parts.note: a T is shaped like a cross
rue is French for street or road

explanation.surface: A question about a French crossroads, answered with approval.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cross-road' looks like crossroads, but the hyphen splits it: Cross gives T and 'road in France' gives RUE.
explanation.definitionFit: True and correct are synonyms, both meaning accurate.

parts.note: surfers here are people browsing the internet, not riding waves, and they visit pages online

explanation.surface: Beaches that wave-riders like to visit.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests beaches, but these surfers ride the web.
explanation.definitionFit: Internet users go to online locations made of linked pages, which is what these are.

parts.note: to air washing is to dry it off, so dry can mean air
CE is the Church of England, a standard abbreviation for church

explanation.surface: A remark that a church service is dry and dull.
explanation.walkthrough: 'church service' looks like one phrase, but the church gives CE and 'service' alone is the definition, as in one of the armed services.
explanation.definitionFit: The armed forces are called the services, and the RAF is one of them.

parts.note: F is the polite stand-in for the swear word a foul-mouthed speaker uses, as in 'the F-word'
lag is slang for a convict, especially an old lag who has served many sentences

explanation.surface: A man named Jack described as a swearing jailbird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jack' looks like a man's name, but it is the flag flown on a ship, as in Union Jack.
explanation.definitionFit: A jack is a small national banner flown at a ship's bow, so it is a kind of standard.

clue.text: Pressing clothes for the ball, maybe

definitions.text: Pressing clothes for the ball, maybe

parts.words: Pressing clothes for the ball, maybe
parts.note: pressing is making smooth or level, and clothes as a verb means dresses, so the phrase reads as smoothing a garment while describing a formal gown

explanation.surface: Ironing an outfit ready to wear to a dance.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as ironing, but pressing is making even and clothes is the verb dresses; the whole is formal wear for a ball.
explanation.definitionFit: Formal attire worn to a ball or other night-time occasion is called by this name.

parts.note: dexter is Latin for right, so a dexterous helper is one on the right side, the trusted assistant

explanation.surface: A nimble assistant.
explanation.walkthrough: Dexterous normally means skilful, but its root dexter means right-hand.
explanation.definitionFit: This phrase means one's most trusted assistant or chief helper.

parts.note: PE, physical education, is the school subject also called games
less as a suffix means without, as in penniless

explanation.surface: Someone miserable because their home has no games to play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like it signals something outside, but it simply gives LESS. Games at British schools means sport, hence PE.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone in despair has given up any expectation of things getting better.

clue.text: Clearly intending to quieten the lot

parts.note: sh is the sound made to quieten someone
the lot means everything, all of it

explanation.surface: Someone plainly planning to hush everybody.
explanation.definitionFit: The auxiliary verb expresses determination or future intention, as in 'we will go'.

indicators.note: in signals that the letters sit inside the run of words charming estaminet

explanation.surface: An invitation to dine in a delightful little French café.
explanation.walkthrough: An estaminet is a small French café or bar, which makes the surface plausible.
explanation.definitionFit: To ingest something is to take it into the body as food, so it means to consume.

clue.text: She wants a year in Morocco

indicators.note: in places the year inside the letters for Morocco

parts.note: MA is the international vehicle registration code for Morocco
YR is the usual abbreviation for year

explanation.surface: A woman who longs to spend twelve months in North Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'She' is the definition: a girl's name stands for any woman in crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: Myra is a female first name, so it can stand for any woman.

clue.text: Somehow fit names into the invoice

indicators.note: somehow suggests the letters of fit names are rearranged in some way

explanation.surface: Squeezing customers' names onto a bill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Somehow' signals the anagram of FIT NAMES.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship's manifest is a list of cargo, effectively an inventory or bill of goods.
A flash is a moment, as in 'in a flash', and also a burst of light used to send a message.

parts.note: fresh means cheeky or forward in making advances, so amorous
a fellow is a man

explanation.surface: A new arrival who turns out to be a ladies' man.
explanation.definitionFit: A freshman is a first-year student, someone new to college.
Tops is slang for the very best, and spinning tops are toys that turn round and round.

clue.text: To play it one needs forbearance

definitions.text: To play it one needs forbearance

parts.words: To play it one needs forbearance
parts.note: the card game played alone shares its name with the quality of calm endurance it requires

explanation.surface: A remark that some game demands tolerance.
explanation.walkthrough: The solitaire card game and the virtue of waiting calmly share one name.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a one-player card game, also called solitaire, and also calm endurance.

clue.text: Bill needs to go back into French resort

indicators.note: into puts the turned word inside the name of the resort

parts.note: Nice is a resort city on the French Riviera

indicators.note: go back tells us the little word to is read in the other direction

explanation.surface: An invoice that has to be taken back to a holiday town in France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bill' looks like a name or an invoice, but it is a posted public sign, as in 'stick no bills'; 'go back' turns the little word round before 'into' places it.
explanation.definitionFit: A bill is a poster or placed announcement, as in 'stick no bills', which is a public sign.

indicators.note: mislaid suggests the letters of a belt Sam have been put in the wrong places

explanation.surface: Sam has lost a belt, and the word belt is repeated.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'Belt' is the definition in the sense of hit hard; the second belt is part of the anagram fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: To belt someone is to thrash them, and to lambaste originally meant to beat soundly.

clue.text: Encountered redhead in charge of this sort of measurement

parts.note: met is the past tense of meet, so encountered
the head of the word red is its first letter, R

explanation.surface: Meeting a ginger-haired person who runs a system of units.
explanation.walkthrough: 'redhead' looks like a ginger person, but it means the first letter of red.
explanation.definitionFit: The metric system measures in metres, litres and grams, based on tens.

clue.text: Craven, so not exactly a fit adherent

indicators.note: not exactly suggests the letters of a fit adherent are not in their exact order

explanation.surface: A coward who is hardly a loyal and robust follower.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not exactly' looks like a mild hedge, but it signals rearranging A FIT ADHERENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Craven means cowardly, lacking in courage or spirit.

indicators.note: utterly is read as when uttered, meaning the word is spoken

parts.note: vain can mean futile or pointless, as idle threats are

explanation.surface: A pin-up who is extremely conceited.
explanation.walkthrough: 'utterly' looks like completely, but here it means as spoken: IDLE said out loud.
explanation.definitionFit: A heart-throb is someone adored by fans, a pop or film star worshipped by them.

clue.text: Hew died shortly after being dismissed

parts.note: to hew is to chop with an axe
D is the short form of died, as in genealogies

explanation.surface: Someone named Hew passed away soon after being sacked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hew' looks like a man's name (Hugh), but it is the verb to chop.
explanation.definitionFit: To be axed is to be sacked, so it means fired from a job.
Mint means brand new, as in mint condition, and a mint is also a large fortune, as in 'it cost a mint'.

clue.text: Bejewelled English silver from times past

parts.note: to stone something is to set it with gems, so bejewelled points to stone
AG is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: Antique silverware from England encrusted with jewels.
explanation.walkthrough: The charade is in answer order: AG comes before E though the clue names English first.
explanation.definitionFit: The Stone Age is the prehistoric era before metal tools, a period long ago.

clue.text: Container may not be accepted by venison producer

indicators.note: accepted by says the second piece is taken inside the first

parts.note: venison is deer meat, so the animal that produces it is the deer
can't means may not or is not able to

explanation.surface: A box that a deer farmer may refuse to take.
explanation.walkthrough: 'may not' stands for the contraction can't, with the apostrophe dropped as crosswords allow.
explanation.definitionFit: A decanter is a glass vessel into which wine or spirits are poured for serving.
